(a) the ESD of $X^\top X$ can be characterized by a fixed point equation, (b) the fixed-point equation is equivalent to an equation that characterizes the ESD of a random matrix with independent entries, (c) this equivalence allows us to derive an efficient algorithm for computing the ESD of the sample covariance matrices, (d) the algorithm is based on a fixed point iteration of the Stieltjies transform, (e) the algorithm is applicable

the Stieltjess transform of the ESD of a sample covariance matrix can be computed by solving a fixed-point equation and that the fixed-point equation can be solved by a fixed-point iteration that converges at an exponential rate.
the limit spectral distribution is the unique solution of the fixed-point equation and the limit distribution of the ESD is the same as that of the Stieltjies transform.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two problems: (i) Given an $n \cdot p$ data matrix, compute the ESD of its sample covariance matrix.
the asymptotic behavior of the eigenvalues of sample covariance matrices and the associated Stieltjes transforms.
the computation of the PSD from the ESD of a sample covariance matrix.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ESD of the sample covariance is a deterministic function of the PSD of the underlying population, with a deterministic mapping that is given by the solution of a fixed point equation.

the limit spectral distribution of the sample covariance of a random vector $x$ is the solution of the fixed point equation $m(z)=m_\Sigma(z)+\frac{1}{n}m(z)^2$, where $m_\Sigma$ is the Stieltjies transform of the population distribution.
the ESD of the sample covariance is close to the PSD in terms of both the first and the second order.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we propose a novel method to compute the ESD of the sample covariance matrices, which is more efficient than the existing methods.
we have proposed a new approach that allows us to compute the ESD of the sample covariance in the limit $p \gg n \gg 1$, and to obtain the limit distribution of the extreme eigenvalues.
, we develop a fast algorithm to approximate the solution to the fixed-point equation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fixed-point equation can be efficiently solved using Newton’s method.
, for any fixed $\gamma >0$, the PSD can be recovered from the ESD with an accuracy that is exponentially small in $n$.
the Stieltjs transform of the ESD converges to the Stieltje transform of the PSD at the rate $1/\sqrt{n}$ and the convergence is uniform on compact subsets of the complex plane.
